rationale: UTF-16LE logs are invisible to grep/ripgrep; converted losslessly with mtime preserved so the preflight ordering signal is unchanged.

precisionNote.whatHappened: Run 1 restored timestamps with Date objects, which hold whole milliseconds, so every converted log lost its sub-millisecond mtime fraction (shift of roughly +0.4 to +0.5 ms).
precisionNote.whyTheToolDidNotCatchIt: Its mtime check compared Date.getTime() on both sides - two ROUNDED values agreeing with each other - so it printed 'mtime drift: 0'.
precisionNote.whyItStillMatters: preflight-freshness.mjs compares statSync().mtimeMs, a FLOAT, so this drift is inside the signal that gate reads.
precisionNote.whyItCannotChangeAGateDecision: The gate compares the newest qualifying log per area against that area's newest source file, and those are separated by seconds or more; a sub-millisecond shift cannot flip that comparison. Verified by the preflight run cited in the ledger, which reports the ordering margins.
precisionNote.fixedHow: The restore now derives fractional SECONDS from mtimeNs and the assertion is mtimeNs equality, so any residual drift FAILS the run instead of passing a rounded comparison. Verified on a probe: node Date truncates 1789327499673.1008 to 1789327499673, while the float-seconds path round-tripped identical nanoseconds.
precisionNote.notRecoverable: The true sub-millisecond fractions of the 116 converted logs are not recoverable; the values recorded below are accurate to the millisecond only.
